rationales: Mastication is the grinding and chewing of food by the teeth.
Lubrication moistens food, mainly with saliva.
Absorption is the uptake of digested nutrients.
Defecation is the elimination of faeces.
Margulis helped develop later classification systems but did not introduce the five-kingdom system.
E. Chatton distinguished prokaryotes from eukaryotes.
Carolus Linnaeus developed an earlier system of classification.
Robert Whittaker introduced the five-kingdom classification system.
Protein synthesis occurs on ribosomes, including those in chloroplasts, but is not the chloroplast’s main function.
Chloroplasts contain DNA, but DNA replication is not their main function.
Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis.
Chloroplasts produce ATP during photosynthesis, but photosynthesis is their broader function.
Chiasmata form during prophase I as crossing-over sites become visible.
Telophase I occurs after homologous chromosomes have separated.
Metaphase I is when homologous chromosome pairs align at the cell equator.
Anaphase I is when homologous chromosomes move to opposite poles.
Karl Lohmann discovered ATP in 1929.
Calvin is known for work on the pathway of carbon fixation in photosynthesis.
Hans Krebs is known for describing the Krebs cycle.
Emil Fischer is known for work on sugars and enzymes.
Albumin helps maintain the osmotic balance of blood.
Globulins include transport and immune proteins.
Hemoglobin transports oxygen in red blood cells.
Fibrinogen is converted into fibrin during blood clotting.
Dr. Abdul Salam is associated with the saying that scientific knowledge is humanity’s common heritage.
Dr. Atta ur Rehman is a Pakistani scientist and science administrator, but this saying is attributed to Abdus Salam.
Dr. Samar Mubarak is known for work in nuclear science, not this saying.
Dr. Abdul Qadeer Khan is known for his work in nuclear technology, not this saying.
Ichthyology is the study of fishes.
Mammalogy is the study of mammals.
Ornithology is the study of birds.
Entomology is the study of insects.
Observations are gathered evidence, not the logical consequences drawn from a hypothesis.
Deduction derives logical consequences from hypotheses.
Summarization condenses information rather than deriving consequences.
Experiments test hypotheses and their predictions.
Folic acid forms coenzymes involved in one-carbon transfers, so it can also act as a coenzyme precursor.
Glycerine is not a vitamin or coenzyme.
Riboflavin is a vitamin that forms the coenzymes FMN and FAD.
Glucose is a sugar, not a vitamin or coenzyme.
The cell wall does not construct ribosomes.
The nucleolus is the site where ribosomal subunits are assembled.
The endoplasmic reticulum may have ribosomes attached, but they are assembled in the nucleolus.
Plastids can contain ribosomes, but they are not the site of ribosome construction.
Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material, not the attachment point.
A bivalent is a paired set of homologous chromosomes.
A chiasma is the point where non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes remain attached.
Metaphase is a stage of cell division, not an attachment point.
Chromatin is the loose, thread-like form of genetic material in the nucleus.
A centromere is the region joining sister chromatids.
Spindle fibres help move chromosomes during cell division.
The nucleolus is a region involved in ribosome production.
Calvin did not first use the term enzyme.
Kühne first used the term enzyme.
Fischer is known for the lock-and-key model of enzyme action.
Daniel Koshland proposed the induced-fit model of enzyme action.
Chlorophyll b is an accessory photosynthetic pigment.
Carotenoids are accessory pigments that absorb additional wavelengths.
Chlorophyll a is the main photosynthetic pigment.
Chlorophyll c is an accessory pigment found in some algae.
